To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
q can be calculated from the Bohr-Lamb formula for gaseous media, and from the Bethe-Born formula for solid targets.

the average charge state of a heavy ion is a function of its initial charge state, q _{i}, its velocity v, the density of the target, n, and the atomic number of the target atoms Z, and can be expressed as q=Q(q _{i},v,n,Z).
q in gaseous and in solid targets is predicted well by Bohr-Lamb criterion, and the influence of density is small.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and application of a theoretical model for the average charge of heavy ions stripped in gases.

the development of a new technique to measure the average equilibrium charge of heavy ions stripped in gases and solids, and with the evaluation of the accuracy of existing theoretical and semi-empirical models to predict the equilibrium charge state.
the study of the interaction of heavy ions with matter.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the average charge state of heavy ions penetrating gaseous or solid targets is determined by the ion velocity and by the target properties, and that the Bohr-Lamb criterion provides a simple and useful method to estimate q in a given target.
the existing semi-empirical and theoretical methods are not yet capable to predict q with sufficient accuracy.
the average charge state of heavy ions in the energy range 0.01-200 MeV/u, and in gaseous and/or solid targets, can be predicted to within 10-15% with the help of the Bohr-Lamb criterion.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the average charge states of heavy ions can be well described by existing semi-empirical models.
the average equilibrium charge of heavy ions is accurately predictable for gaseous targets, but not for solids.

the Bohr-Lamb criterion gives a very good description of q for gaseous targets, while for solid targets a semi-empirical method based on a combination of the Bohr-Lambs criterion and the Thomas-Fermi-Dirac theory of atomic structure gives a good description of q.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the average charge state q of heavy ions can be predicted with good accuracy in a large energy range and for different target materials.
, for a given ion, the charge state is determined by the ion velocity, the density of the medium, and the ion-target interaction potential.
there is no single method which is applicable for all energies and all target materials.
